name: 08_queue_drains_in_order
why: The queue is what makes a failed write a DELAY instead of a loss, so its ordering is memory ordering: turns must reach AnhurDB oldest-first, and each one must land in ITS OWN session. The two implementations sort by file name and both encode a sortable UTC stamp in that name, which is the shared rule under test. Items a and c belong to one conversation and b to another - if a drain ever collapses them into one session it breaks the inviolable rule `1 agent session = 1 AnhurDB session`.
on_failure: Order wrong => recovered memories are replayed out of sequence. A `@` suffix that does not match the item's own session => a cross-conversation merge, the failure the whole session-first design exists to prevent. Anything left in pending_after => the drain did not actually deliver.
